sections.heading: 1. Who is the controller of your data
body:
The controller of your personal data within the meaning of the GDPR is:
Zakład Graficzny Maciej Godek
ul. Cumownicza 1a/2
60-480 Poznań, Poland
VAT ID (NIP): 7831780263
Avably is a project run by this controller.
Contact for all data-related matters: admin@avably.io
The controller has not appointed a Data Protection Officer.

sections.heading: 2. What this policy covers
body: This policy covers only the avably.io website and waitlist sign-ups. Avably has not yet launched as a service - when it does, we will publish a separate policy for the product.

sections.heading: 3. What data we collect
body:
When you join the waitlist, we collect:
- your email address (required),
- the type of equipment you rent, the size of your inventory, and how you currently manage bookings - that is, your answers in the form,
- details about the equipment - only if you choose “other”,
- whether you want to take part in the pilot,
- your phone number - only if you apply for the pilot. Without that application, the form will not accept a phone number at all,
- the time when you give consent,
- the language in which you view the website,
- campaign identifiers (the utm_source and utm_campaign parameters in the address), if you reached us through a campaign link.
We do not save your IP address with your submission. We use it only temporarily to limit the number of submissions from one address and protect the form against abuse. The key expires automatically.

sections.heading: 4. Why we use the data and on what legal basis
body:
- Adding you to the waitlist and sending information about the development and launch of Avably - based on your consent (Article 6(1)(a) GDPR).
- Contacting you about the pilot - based on your consent, if you express such an interest.
- Protecting the form against abuse - based on our legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR).
We use answers about equipment type and inventory only to understand who we are building the product for. We do not make any automated decisions based on them and we do not profile you.

sections.heading: 5. Who processes data on our behalf
body:
We use providers that process data on our behalf:
- Supabase - submission database - European Union (Frankfurt)
- Vercel - website hosting - European Union (Frankfurt)
- Upstash - protection of the form against abuse - European Union (Frankfurt)
- Cloudflare - DNS and website protection - global network
- Resend - sending messages to you - European Union

We store data in the European Union. Some of these companies are based in the United States, so technical support may involve transferring data outside the European Economic Area. This takes place on the basis of standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission.
We do not sell your data or share it with anyone for marketing purposes.

sections.heading: 6. How long we keep the data
body: Until you withdraw your consent, but no longer than 24 months after you join. After you withdraw consent, we delete your submission.

sections.heading: 7. Your rights
body: You have the right to access your data, correct it, delete it, restrict its processing, transfer it, object to processing based on our legitimate interest, and withdraw your consent at any time. Withdrawing consent does not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out before the withdrawal.
To exercise these rights, write to admin@avably.io. We will respond within one month at the latest.
You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (Prezes Urzędu Ochrony Danych Osobowych), ul. Stawki 2, 00-193 Warsaw, Poland.

sections.heading: 8. Cookies
body: The website uses one functional cookie that remembers the language you selected. It is necessary for the language switcher to work and is not used for tracking.
We do not use analytics or marketing cookies and we do not track you on other websites. If this changes, we will update this policy and ask for your consent before enabling any tracking.

sections.heading: 9. Is providing data mandatory
body: No. Joining the waitlist is entirely voluntary. However, without an email address we cannot add you to the list.

sections.heading: 10. Changes to this policy
body: If we change this policy, we will publish a new version on this page and change the date at the top. We will notify you by email about material changes.

banner.text: 14 days to try it, no card. No Avably cut on bookings and no per-user limits.

hero.titleBottom: You run everything else in one place.
hero.body: Avably connects your rental website to an operations back office. A booking goes straight into the calendar and order list; from there, the same team prepares the equipment, hands it over or ships it, takes the return and settles the deposit. No retyping between forms, spreadsheets and messages.
hero.feature2: Payment and deposit tied to the booking
hero.posterAlt: A sectional door pulled down moments before opening, a narrow strip of daylight underneath

premise.statement: A booking starts the work; it does not finish it. The equipment still has to be prepared, handed over or shipped, returned on time and checked. Sometimes you price an extension, sometimes you deduct PLN 57 for cleaning, and every deposit must end at zero. Avably keeps those steps on one order, so the team can see what happened and what comes next.
premise.feature1: One order through the full rental cycle
premise.feature3: Store, payment and back office in one workflow

branze.title: The same workflow, different equipment
branze.note: Avably fits rental businesses that charge by the day and need to track specific units. Product names change; booking, handover, return and deposit do not. You start the website from one of six ready-made templates.
branze.item1Alt: A concrete mixer and buckets on a site in a room under renovation
branze.item2Alt: A set of spanners and hex keys laid out on a workshop board
branze.item3Alt: Dozens of identical chairs stacked in a warehouse
branze.item4Alt: Two stage spotlights against an orange background
branze.item5Alt: A row of identical bicycle wheels with red rims

tabs.title: See one order move through Avably
tabs.item1Body: Your store starts at yourname.avably.io, and you can add your own domain later. Build the page from ready-made sections and one of six templates. The draft is visible only to you; customers get the version you deliberately publish.
tabs.item2Title: Customers book without waiting for a call
tabs.item2Body: In the store, a customer picks the equipment and dates, sees the rental price and deposit, then pays by card, bank transfer or on pickup. The server confirms both price and availability. The finished order lands in the back office and you both receive a confirmation.
tabs.item3Title: Plan the day around available units
tabs.item3Body: The calendar counts individual units and includes live rentals, buffers and servicing. You can see what goes out today, what should return and what needs preparing for tomorrow. If two people choose the last free unit, only one booking can go through.
tabs.item4Title: Hand it over or ship it
tabs.item4Body: Pickup and delivery stay on the same order. For a courier shipment, create the parcel, download the PDF label and keep the tracking number next to the equipment and dates - not in a separate inbox.
tabs.item5Title: Take the return and settle the deposit
tabs.item5Body: The register records PLN 950 collected, PLN 57 deducted for cleaning, the remainder refunded and a zero balance - each with its date and reason. After a card payment, one action sends the refund back to the card; for cash or bank transfer, you record the settlement yourself. If the customer asks about PLN 57, the answer sits on the order.

video.quote: I run a rental business myself. Avably grew out of the days when two people arrived for the same piece of equipment and the deposit trail lived somewhere in the phone.
video.authorRole: founder of Avably, runs a rental business

features.title: Everything supporting the rental between those steps
features.card1Title: Tiered pricing and extensions without a calculator
features.card1Body: Set a price for a day, a week or a longer rental. Moving the dates reprices the full order, while an extension adds the difference without manually rebuilding each line.
features.card2Title: Online payments with no Avably cut
features.card2Body: Customers pay by card on your website and the money reaches your own account with the payment provider. Avably charges a subscription, not a percentage of bookings. BLIK and Przelewy24 are being built, with no promised date.
features.card3Title: Customer, history and decisions on the order
features.card3Body: The customer record gathers orders and invoice details. Notes carry an author and a date, so the team sees what was agreed. Block someone you do not want to serve again by both email address and phone number.
features.card4Title: Agreement, messages and invoice in one trail
features.card4Body: Order data becomes a PDF rental agreement. Lifecycle emails go out in the customer's language and keep their delivery result. You still issue the invoice outside Avably, but you can send it from the back office and keep that trail. Automatic invoicing is still only on the Premium list.
features.card5Title: Bookings on the website you already have
features.card5Body: Embed the calendar with a script or the WordPress plugin. In that setup, customers pay by bank transfer or on pickup. A public API can power your own interface while every order still lands in the same back office.

cta.title: Start with what is happening today
cta.body: The dashboard puts check-outs, returns, overdue orders, tomorrow's preparation and money alerts into five fixed tiles. Every item opens the relevant order. Revenue, trends and equipment utilisation stay below as context for a decision, not another list to maintain.

momentum.title: From an empty account to the first booking
momentum.card1Title: Open an account and name the store
momentum.card1Body: Confirm your email, create the organisation and choose the store address. No installation, sales call or card. The back office immediately gives you a short checklist of what is needed to open.
momentum.card2Body: Products and tiered prices come in from a CSV file. Add units, pickup points and photos in the back office. A larger inventory takes real time, so you can work in stages and publish the part of the offer that is ready.
momentum.card3Title: Publish and run the first rental
momentum.card3Body: A customer books on the website and the order appears on the list. From there, run it through preparation, handover, return and deposit. Invite the next members of the team by email.

security.title: See how we guard the data
security.card1Title: The database itself separates rental data
security.card1Body: The wall between two businesses sits in the database itself (Row Level Security), not in the screens above it. A test guards it on every change to the system: it deliberately reaches for another business's rows and has to be refused, or the change does not ship.
security.card2Title: We never hold a card number
security.card2Body: Payments run through Stripe - card numbers never touch our servers and are never stored here. We do not collect national ID numbers or scans of identity documents either. A name, an email, a phone, an address and a tax number for the invoice is all we keep.
security.card3Body: The database, the hosting and the mail all run in EU regions. Courier integration keys are encrypted separately for each business, and the key we encrypt them with does not live in the database.
security.card4Title: We cannot get into the platform without a code
security.card4Body: Our own administrative access needs a second factor (TOTP) - a password alone gets none of us in. Store and back-office pages ship a Content-Security-Policy computed separately for each request, plus HSTS and the rest of the security headers.
security.card5Title: An address for reporting holes, and the GDPR paperwork
security.card5Body: We publish security.txt (RFC 9116) with an address for vulnerability reports. We do not yet have a data processing agreement or self-service deletion of a customer's data; both are being written before the paid plans start.
security.note: We hold no external certifications and we do not imply otherwise. Everything above can be checked in the running system.

faq.q1: Can a customer book and pay on my site?
faq.a1: The customer picks the equipment and the days, sees live availability and pays by card - the deposit comes off with the order. Our server works out the amount; the customer's browser never touches it. Anyone who prefers the old way pays by transfer or on pickup. BLIK and Przelewy24 are being built - we are not giving dates.
faq.q2: What do I pay, and do you take a cut of each booking?
faq.a2Lead: PLN 199 net a month, and no cut.
faq.a2: That price covers the back office, the store website and online payments. We do not count users or orders. A year up front costs the same as ten months. We take nothing from the transaction: the money goes straight to your own account with the payment provider, and you sign that contract yourself, so their rates come from them, not through us. Premium at PLN 399 net is on the page, but we are not selling it yet.
faq.a3: You sign up without a card, so there is nothing for us to charge - after fourteen days nothing happens by itself. The prices are set: Standard at PLN 199 net a month, Premium at PLN 399 net, a year for the price of ten months, no annual contract and no onboarding fee. Subscription payment goes live before the commercial launch - we will email you before anything starts costing money. Catalogue, orders and customers export to CSV whenever you want.
faq.q4: My bookings live in a notebook and a spreadsheet. How do I move them?
faq.a4Lead: The catalogue goes in as a CSV.
faq.a4: The file uses our column layout, so the simplest way is to export the empty one and fill it in. Before anything is saved you get a preview: how many items will be added, how many overwritten, and which row has an error. Photos, units and pickup points you add in the back office, because the CSV does not carry them. The import covers the catalogue, not bookings - open dates you enter by hand. Export works the other way round, so your data is not locked in here.
faq.q5: Can the store run on my own domain?
faq.a5: The moment your organisation exists, the store already answers at yourname.avably.io, so you have something to show customers on day one. Your own domain goes on whenever you want: the back office spells out the record (type, name, value), you paste it at your registrar and press “Check verification”. DNS is sometimes ready in minutes, sometimes hours. No developer needed.
faq.q6: Who is Avably a bad fit for?
faq.a6: We price rentals in days, off tiered day rates - hours are simply not something we count. We do not run retail either: tills, receipts and stock to sell belong in a different program. Flats and premises are outside this entirely. And there is nobody here who will load your catalogue for you - you sign up and click through it yourself, and we answer email, usually the same business day.
faq.q7: Can another rental business see my data?
faq.a7: The boundary sits in the database, not in what the screen draws. On every change to the code a test deliberately reaches for another business's rows and tries to change them. It has to be refused, or the change does not ship. Admin access to the platform itself takes a second factor. We never see card numbers at all, because Stripe holds them.
faq.q8: Where does my data sit, and what about GDPR?
faq.a8: The database, the hosting and the email run with providers whose servers are in the EU. We keep ordinary contact details of your customers: name, email, phone, address, tax number for the invoice. We do not collect national ID numbers or scans of ID documents. You are the controller of that data; we process it on your instruction. The data processing agreement and self-service deletion of a customer record do not exist yet - both land before the paid plans start.

pricingPage.metadataDescription: Compare Avably plans: 14 days without a card, a flat subscription and no cut of your bookings.
pricingPage.title: Pay a subscription, not a cut of every booking
pricingPage.intro: Prices are net; 23% VAT is added on the invoice. 14-day trial, no card. A year up front costs ten instalments instead of twelve, on either plan.
pricingPage.standardYearly: Yearly: PLN 1,990 net. That is PLN 398 less than twelve monthly payments.
pricingPage.standardNote: Everything on this list works today. Check it yourself on the trial, before you pay anything.
pricingPage.s1: A booking calendar that shows free units, and a service window that keeps equipment out of the pool after an inspection
pricingPage.s2: With a card payment the deposit comes off with the order and you give it back in one click; with cash or a transfer you record the collection and the refund yourself, with the amount and the reason for any deduction
pricingPage.s3: The customer pays by card on your site; we take no cut of the transaction (BLIK and Przelewy24 being built)
pricingPage.s4: You send and take back shipments by courier, print the PDF label from the back office, and price delivery from your own rate card
pricingPage.s5: A store site with the editor and your own domain, or the widget and WordPress plugin on the site you already run (there: bank transfer and payment on pickup for now)
pricingPage.s6: A PDF rental agreement, and on every order you can see which customer email went out and which did not
pricingPage.s7: No cap on users, orders or products - the whole crew costs the same
pricingPage.premiumYearly: Yearly: PLN 3,990 net. Twelve monthly payments would come to PLN 4,788.
pricingPage.premiumNote: Everything in Standard, plus a list on which nothing works yet. That is why we are not selling it: sales open when the first item ships. No dates.
pricingPage.p1: Check-out and check-in protocols: photos of the equipment stay on the order
pricingPage.p2: The rental agreement signed on screen, no printer involved
pricingPage.p3: The invoice issues itself once the order is paid, and goes to KSeF
pricingPage.p4: Seasonal and weekend rates, without editing the price list every Friday
pricingPage.p5: Paid damage cover in the customer's basket: revenue you do not have today
pricingPage.p6: Customer emails go out from your domain instead of ours
pricingPage.p7: Higher public API limits; your tickets go to the front of the queue
pricingPage.honest1: There is no onboarding fee and no annual contract - and nothing to onboard: you open the account by email and click through it yourself. We never take a card, so nothing charges itself after 14 days; subscription payment goes live before the commercial launch, and we will tell you by email first.
pricingPage.honest2: We do not sell the Premium list until it works. We show it so you know where the product is going, and can tell us the order is wrong. And your data sits separated from every other business in the database itself, not on the screen - a test checks that on every change to the system.
